title: Uncertainty-aware Generative Recommendation

problem.claim: Generative recommendation reformulates recommendation as end-to-end autoregressive sequence generation, but preference optimization methods commonly rely on binary outcome correctness.

gap.claim: Existing methods neglect generation confidence, variation in sample learning difficulty, and explicit confidence expression, causing unstable training dynamics and unquantifiable decision risks.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes UGR, a unified framework that uses uncertainty as a signal for adaptive optimization.
UGR combines uncertainty-weighted rewards that penalize confident errors with difficulty-aware optimization dynamics intended to prevent premature convergence.
UGR adds explicit confidence alignment to enable confidence expression and support downstream risk-aware applications.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report superior recommendation performance in extensive experiments.
The authors report that UGR stabilizes training and prevents performance degradation observed with standard methods.
The authors report that learned confidence enables reliable downstream risk-aware applications.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative recommendation is framed as end-to-end autoregressive sequence generation.
Binary-outcome preference optimization is described as uncertainty-blind, neglecting confidence, difficulty variation, and confidence expression.
UGR addresses the limitation through uncertainty-weighted rewards, difficulty-aware optimization, and confidence alignment.
The authors report improved recommendation performance, more stable training, and risk-aware downstream utility.
A project repository is reported as available.

source_observation.claim: The framework treats uncertainty as an optimization signal and separately addresses confident errors, sample difficulty, and confidence expression.

interpretation.claim: Recommendation optimization may benefit from modeling both prediction reliability and learning difficulty rather than optimizing binary correctness alone.

application.claim: This pattern could inform systems that need calibrated outputs or risk-aware recommendation decisions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which settings, datasets, or failure modes limit the reported benefits.

unknowns: No datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results are specified.
Implementation details and ablation results are not provided.
Calibration quality and the scope of downstream risk-aware applications are unspecified.
